tasks.q: Which is the best variable name for a running total of scores?
a: totalScore
x
t1
thisVariableStoresTheTotalOfAllTheScoresSoFar
tasks.fb: A good name is descriptive but still short. Single letters don't say what the data is, and very long names are hard to read.

tasks.q: Why do descriptive variable names make code easier to maintain?
a: Anyone reading the code can tell what data each variable holds
They make the program run faster
They use less memory
The translator needs them to understand the code
tasks.fb: The computer doesn't care what a variable is called. Good names are for the humans who read and update the code.

tasks.q: What is the purpose of a comment?
a: To explain what a section of code does, for anyone reading it
To make the code run
To stop errors happening
To validate the user's input
tasks.fb: Comments explain the code to people. They are especially useful at the start of each sub-program.

tasks.q: What happens to comments when a program is run?
a: They are ignored by the translator
They are printed on the screen
They slow down every line of code
They are checked for logic errors
tasks.fb: Comments are skipped when the code is translated, so they don't change how the program behaves.

a: Which lines belong inside a loop, selection statement or sub-program
Which lines are comments
Which lines contain errors
The order the lines were written in
tasks.fb: Indented lines are inside the structure above them, so you can see the program's structure at a glance. In Python it is required.

tasks.q: Which is the best use of white space?
a: Blank lines between sub-programs and sections of code
No spaces anywhere, to keep the file small
Spaces inside variable names
A blank line after every single line
tasks.fb: Separating sections makes code quicker to scan without spreading it out so much that it's hard to follow.

tasks.q: What is a benefit of using sub-programs?
a: Code can be reused without being copied, and each part tested separately
They remove the need for any testing
They make every program shorter than 10 lines
They stop users entering invalid data
tasks.fb: Procedures and functions are written once and called whenever they're needed, and each one can be tested on its own.

tasks.q: The same 10 lines appear in five places and contain a bug. How would a sub-program have helped?
a: The bug would only need fixing once, in the sub-program
The bug would fix itself
The program would crash less often
It wouldn't help at all
tasks.fb: With the code in one sub-program, one fix corrects every place it's used. Copies mean five fixes, and it's easy to miss one.

a: Techniques that make code easier to debug, update and maintain
Making a program run as fast as possible
Keeping a program secret from other programmers
Testing a program once it is finished
tasks.fb: This is the key terminology definition: maintainable code is easy for anyone to understand, fix and change.

tasks.q: Why is maintainability especially important in large projects?
a: Many programmers work on the code, often for years, so others must be able to understand it
Large projects never need updating
Computers can only run readable code
It makes the program use less storage
tasks.fb: In big projects the person fixing the code is rarely the person who wrote it, and they may be working on it years later.

tasks.q: Which changes would make the locker code program more robust? Select all that apply.
opts: Check the house letter is exactly 1 letter from A to D
Check the form group is a number
Check the year group is a whole number from 7 to 11
Check the seat number is a whole number from 1 to 30
Print the code in capital letters
Remove the prompts to save space
correct: Check the house letter is exactly 1 letter from A to D
Check the form group is a number
Check the year group is a whole number from 7 to 11
Check the seat number is a whole number from 1 to 30
tasks.fb: Each input needs validating before it is used. Changing the output's capitals or removing prompts doesn't make the program more robust.

tasks.q: A student types 'nine' as their year group. Which check would stop this?
a: A type check
A length check
A presence check
A format check
tasks.fb: A type check makes sure the input is a whole number. A range check would then make sure it is between 11 and 19.

info.title: Read more than written
info.text: Programmers spend much more time reading existing code than writing new code; it's often quoted as around 10 times more. That's why readable code saves so much time.

info.title: Python's style guide
info.text: Python has an official style guide called PEP 8. It recommends snake_case for variable and function names, like total_score, and 4 spaces for each level of indentation.

info.title: Indentation in Python
info.text: In most languages indentation is just for readability. In Python it's part of the syntax: the translator uses it to work out which lines are inside a loop or if statement.

info.title: The millennium bug
info.text: Old programs saved space by storing years as two digits, like 99. Before the year 2000, programmers worldwide had to find and fix this code, which was much harder where it was badly documented.

info.title: Really big code
info.text: The Linux operating system kernel has tens of millions of lines of code, written by thousands of developers. Without naming conventions, comments and sub-programs, nobody could maintain it.

info.title: Sanitising input
info.text: As well as validating input, programs often sanitise it first: removing extra spaces or converting to lower case, so ' SMITH ' and 'smith' are treated the same.
